RydAR/How RydAR works

How RydAR works

What goes into a curve warning.

A bend’s shape is a starting point, not a complete picture of driving conditions. RydAR combines mapped road geometry with your position to identify curves ahead and calculate a suggested speed.

Explore the Arkansas map ↗

Arkansas road geometry

The statewide curve database is built from the Arkansas GIS Office’s ROADS_ACF road layer. RydAR identifies bends in the road centerlines and records measurements such as radius and deflection angle. The public web map shows the county-class road portion of that inventory.

This is a computed dataset, not a field survey of every curve. Road geometry, surface labels, and road names can be incomplete or out of date. Loops, ramps, and very tight corners are filtered from the public map.

The suggested speed calculation

The base formula is V = √(15 × R × (e + f)), where V is miles per hour, R is radius in feet, e is assumed road banking, and f is an assumed friction value. The public map calculates a range using banking from −0.02 to +0.02 and friction of 0.15 for paved roads or 0.10 for unpaved roads.

For example, a mapped 300-foot paved curve gives a base range of about 24–27 mph, rounded down. The phone’s tire-tread setting can lower the assumed friction further. These assumptions are not a measurement of the grip available to your tires on that road.

The iPhone’s spoken advisory uses the low end of its calculated range. Neither the map range nor the app advisory is a posted speed limit or an official traffic-engineering recommendation. Follow signs and choose a speed appropriate to current conditions.

Matching the road ahead

The iPhone app checks your position and direction against nearby curves. A bend far to the side of the line of travel is treated as another road. A warning only plays when there is enough road left before the curve; it stays silent once the car is moving away or the bend is too close.

The base lead is 12 seconds of travel, clamped to 100–450 meters. The optional camera check can identify a change in road surface and move a warning earlier. It does not turn a camera frame into a new advisory speed.

Limits to keep in mind

GPS errors can affect road matching. Missing data can leave a bend unmarked. Ice, water, gravel, poor sight distance, tire condition, and vehicle differences can make a computed speed unsuitable. RydAR does not guarantee a warning for every curve or that any particular speed is safe.

Use the map guide to plan while parked, or read about the iPhone beta. Implementation details are available in the speed calculation source and Arkansas database builder.
